nodes.name: HPHT synthesis of CoNiB
nodes.procedure: CoNiB was synthesized under 5 GPa and at 1300 °C using Co and Ni precursors (further details can be found in the experimental method section in the ESI†).
nodes.source_text: Ni₂B and Fe/Ni doped Ni₂B were synthesized under 5 GPa and at 1300 °C...

The electrocatalytic performance of all three TMNiB samples is tested with a standard three electrode system in 1 M KOH solution... FeNiB exhibits the best OER performance with a quite low overpotential of 257 mV at current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... FeNiB also exhibits the lowest Tafel slope of 110 mV dec⁻¹... C_dl is obtained by cyclic voltammetry (CV) at different scan rates (20-100 mV s⁻¹) in a non-faradaic region (0.1–0.2 V vs. Hg/HgO)

Overall water splitting is also tested using nickel foam loaded samples as the anode and Pt foil as the cathode... FeNiB also exhibits the best performance of water splitting with a potential of 1.54 V at 10 mA cm⁻² current density
Fig. 3c shows the chronoamperometry curve obtained at 100 mA cm⁻² current density. After a 30-h test, the potential increases by only 7% for FeNiB
The initial and 10 000 cycled LSV curves for FeNiB are shown in Fig. 3d. Only slight loss of the catalytic activity of FeNiB can be observed

nodes.characterization_summary: Rietveld refinements provide detailed cell parameters and bond lengths; a/c value increases linearly with doping element radii; TM-B bond lengths longer in FeNiB (weaker bond strength).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Rietveld refinements (Fig. S2†) are also performed to obtain detailed information about the cell parameters and bond lengths.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images after ball-milling show morphology; EDS mapping confirms homogeneous Fe/Ni distribution and stoichiometric ratio close to 1:1 for FeNiB/CoNiB.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images after ball-milling for 10 h at 350 rpm are shown in (Fig. S3a–c†). Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping (Fig. S3d and e†) shows a highly homogeneous distribution of Fe and Ni elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiB lattice fringe of 0.2497 nm corresponds to (200) crystal planes of Ni2B (0.2495 nm); SAED reflects highly ordered single-crystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image (Fig. 1e) and selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Fig. 1e inset) pattern of FeNiB reflect the highly ordered single-crystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows highly homogeneous distribution of Fe and Ni elements in FeNiB; stoichiometric ratio Fe:Ni close to 1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping (Fig. 1f) shows a highly homogeneous distribution of elements, consistent with SEM and TEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiB shows Fe-B peak at 706.84 eV, Fe-O at 711.33/724.44 eV; Ni-B at 852.77/870.07 eV; B1s at 188.15/192.00 eV; Ni 2p binding energy shifts higher by 0.25 eV compared to Ni2B.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak located at 706.84 eV is indexed to the Fe–B bond... The peaks located at 852.77 eV and 870.07 eV are assigned to Ni–B bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows electron transfer from metals to borons; increased absorption-edge energies and binding energies of Ni in FeNiB and CoNiB compared to Ni2B.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is performed to comprehend the electronic interaction of different metal elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER TEM of FeNiB shows obvious oxidation layer; HRTEM reveals disordered nano-crystalline Ni(OH)2 (lattice 0.272 nm, (100) facet) particles <10 nm with grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in TEM images (Fig. 6a and b), there is an obvious oxidation layer on the surface of FeNiB after the 30 h OER durability test.
